provenance: Initial calibration from arbiter-confirmed production bans, Jul–Sep 2026 (one panel-research platform; quorum/arbiter confirmation, a few hundred cases double-reviewed by humans). Each weight is a log-likelihood ratio LLR = logit(precision) − logit(prior), capped at ±4.5 so that no single signal can block. Entries marked "assumed" are placeholders for signals without a production measurement. Refit on your own labels with `npm run calibration:fit`. Thresholds: block only at posterior ≥ 0.95 — a block is meant to be a near-certain call that needs no second look; review at ≥ 0.20 — review is cheap, so a signal whose production precision is 20–30 % (e.g. gibberish) still asks for a second look. Everything between 0.20 and 0.95 goes to the review layer (arbiter, then a person). v1.1.0 adds matrix-pattern.straightline_full and widens the heavy_pattern / random_sort routes so that a pattern spanning the whole survey (the long-string / insufficient-effort index of Curran 2016 and Meade & Craig 2012) counts as strong evidence on its own, not only when it is also fast.
